name: MathConstruct
description: A benchmark of 127 challenging mathematical competition problems specifically targeting constructive proofs — problems requiring the construction of mathematical objects with specific properties (e.g., 'construct a sequence such that...'). Fills a major gap in math benchmarks which have focused on calculation and proof verification but not construction. State-of-the-art LLMs solve only 41% of problems.
evaluation_method: accuracy (correctness of constructed mathematical object verified by validators)
reputation: Published at ICML 2025; first benchmark focused on constructive mathematical reasoning; fills gap in evaluating a distinct mathematical skill; automated verification via mathematical validators
notes: ICML 2025. Constructive proofs are distinct from proof verification or calculation — they require generating a valid mathematical object satisfying given constraints. Examples: construct a graph with specific properties, find a sequence satisfying conditions, build a combinatorial object. Automated validation verifies that proposed constructions are actually correct, enabling reproducible evaluation. Covers combinatorics, number theory, algebra, and graph theory.
